rv.q: If you like wartime stories, James Bond movies and appreciate goofiness, “Operation Mincemeat” will make for a very juicy night out.
"Operation Mincemeat" is amazingly well conceived as a stage spectacle.
Operation Mincemeat is an absolute smash.
This is among the best shows out there right now, and one that will stay with me for a long time.
Operation Mincemeat is a riot, one of funniest productions I've seen to date.
It will make you laugh out loud while also feeling heart-tugging emotion for these characters.
Operation Mincemeat emerges as one of the most entertaining touring musicals to play a Mirvish stage in years.
Operation Mincemeat has been hyped incessantly for over a year, and it absolutely lives up to the hype.
And it’s a damn delight—whip-smart, funny, ironic, and completely capable of tugging at the heartstrings at the right moment.
“Operation Mincemeat” feels much broader and more complex than you may think that the modest-in-numbers ensemble might be capable of delivering.
The Broadway-smash musical comedy is a triumph of humor and heart at the Emerson Colonial in Boston.
Rounding off an intelligent production that will leave audiences thinking as well as in stitches.
The show succeeds at taking a serious subject, World War Two, and finding the comedy in the outrageous scheme to fool Hitler and win the war.
A terrifically written and conceived show, with amazing acting, singing, choreography and staging.
You won’t soon forget this musical, and that can’t be said about quite a few of the other offerings at PPAC this season.
A musical with five actors playing over 80 different characters can't help but be impressive and entertaining.
It all amounts to low-fi, highly imaginative Lovecraftian lunacy, created and performed by one of the Toronto theatre scene’s true originals.
A corpse, a preposterous plan, and five tireless performers make this British spy caper an enormously funny exercise in controlled chaos.
Mirvish's wildly entertaining ‘Operation Mincemeat’ is one of the best musicals since ‘Hamilton’...
But this touring production feels like a copy of a copy: louder, broader, and far less able to carry the weight of its own concept.
If you are ready to have a blast at the theater while learning a little history, then make a date to see this show before it leaves.

cn.t: Critics praise this inventive British musical about a WWII deception scheme as witty, irreverent, and enormously entertaining, with five tireless performers playing 80+ characters. Most find it a triumph of humor and heart, though a few note execution falls short.
